**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** **Topic 1.** You have passed your entrance examination into one of the prominent universities in Cameroon. Many of your friends do not share in your happiness because they do not like to study in Cameroon. They think that one can only succeed if one goes abroad. Write a speech in which you convince them about studies in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect strict du format imposé (discours, essai d'opinion, lettre formelle) que le contenu : un contenu excellent rédigé dans le mauvais format perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Un discours s'adresse directement à un auditoire (apostrophe, formules d'appel, ton persuasif) ; un essai d'opinion présente une position claire dès l'introduction, développée par des arguments organisés, puis une conclusion qui la réaffirme ; une lettre formelle respecte l'en-tête, la formule d'appel, les paragraphes structurés et la formule de politesse propres à la correspondance administrative anglaise. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen : les trois modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois formats attendus.

## Topic 1 - Speech (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Dear friends,

I stand before you today not simply to celebrate my own success, but to address something that troubles me: your belief that success only exists beyond our borders. I understand your doubts, but I ask you to consider a few things with me.

First, a university is only as valuable as the effort a student puts into it. Many of Cameroon's most respected doctors, engineers and professors were trained right here, in institutions that many of you dismiss without ever setting foot in them. Excellence is not imported; it is built through discipline, curiosity and hard work, wherever one happens to study.

Second, studying in Cameroon means learning in a context that understands our realities: our history, our languages, our challenges. This makes what we learn immediately useful to the people around us, rather than knowledge that must first be translated into a foreign context before it becomes relevant here.

Third, staying here does not mean staying still. Many Cameroonian universities now offer exchange programmes, international partnerships and scholarships that open the same doors abroad, once we have proven ourselves at home.

I am not asking you to close your eyes to opportunities elsewhere. I am asking you to stop believing that a Cameroonian degree is worth less than a foreign one simply because of where it was earned. Success is a personal achievement, not a stamp on a passport.

I hope you will join me in celebrating not just my results, but the opportunity I have been given to prove this point, right here, in Cameroon.

Thank you.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** **Topic 2.** There is a lot of emphasis on Mother Tongue Education these days. Many schools have instituted the teaching and learning of these languages. What is your stand on this?
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Opinion essay (modèle, environ 260 mots)

I strongly support the growing emphasis on Mother Tongue Education in Cameroonian schools, because a language carries far more than words: it carries the history, values and identity of the community that speaks it.

To begin with, children who start their education in a language they already speak fluently at home understand new concepts more easily than those forced to learn everything in a second or third language from the very first day. Studies on early education consistently show that a strong foundation in one's mother tongue actually makes it easier, not harder, to later master other languages such as French or English.

Furthermore, many of Cameroon's mother tongues are spoken by shrinking numbers of people, especially among the youth, who increasingly favour official languages in daily life. Teaching these languages in schools is one of the few remaining ways to keep them alive for future generations, before they disappear entirely along with the oral traditions, proverbs and songs they carry.

Some argue that focusing on local languages might distract students from mastering French or English, which remain essential for national and international communication. However, mother tongue education, as currently implemented, complements rather than replaces the official languages: it is added to the curriculum, not substituted for it.

For all these reasons, I believe schools are right to teach and encourage the use of mother tongues, and I would encourage even more institutions to follow this example across the country.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** **Topic 3.** Multi-media centers have been created in many secondary schools in Cameroon. You are the president of the Students' Association and you would like your school to be equipped with these materials and trained teachers. Write a letter to the Minister of Secondary Education to this effect. Your name is NDONGO Nebi and the name of your school is GSS Nso in the Centre Region of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Formal letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

GSS Nso
Centre Region
Cameroon

The Minister of Secondary Education
Yaoundé

Subject: Request for the installation of a multi-media center at GSS Nso

Dear Sir,

I am writing to you in my capacity as President of the Students' Association of GSS Nso, in the Centre Region of Cameroon, to request your support in equipping our school with a multi-media center and trained teaching staff.

Many secondary schools across Cameroon have already benefited from such centers, which give students hands-on experience with computers and digital tools that are now essential in almost every field of study and employment. Our school, unfortunately, still lacks this equipment, which places our students at a clear disadvantage compared to their peers in better-equipped institutions.

We believe that a multi-media center at GSS Nso would greatly improve the quality of teaching and learning, particularly in subjects that increasingly rely on digital resources, and would better prepare our students for further studies and for the modern job market.

I would therefore be most grateful if you could consider our school among those to benefit from this program, and if possible, arrange for the training of teachers who would be responsible for supervising this equipment.

Thank you for your attention to this request. I look forward to your favourable response.

Yours faithfully,

NDONGO Nebi
President, Students' Association, GSS Nso

### Piège à éviter
L'erreur la plus fréquente sur cette section est de confondre les registres : rédiger la lettre au ministre avec un ton trop familier, ou au contraire rédiger le discours avec un ton trop administratif et impersonnel. Une autre erreur fréquente sur le sujet 3 est d'oublier les éléments obligatoires d'une lettre formelle anglaise (adresse de l'expéditeur, adresse du destinataire, objet, formule d'appel "Dear Sir/Madam", formule de politesse finale "Yours faithfully" ou "Yours sincerely") : leur absence est systématiquement sanctionnée, même si le contenu de la lettre est par ailleurs excellent.

### Conseil
Avant de commencer à écrire le jour de l'examen, note en quelques mots au brouillon la structure attendue du format choisi (par exemple pour la lettre : adresses, objet, appel, corps en 2-3 paragraphes, formule finale, signature) : cette liste de contrôle, relue une dernière fois juste avant de rendre la copie, évite d'oublier un élément formel qui coûte des points indépendamment de la qualité du contenu.

incertitudes: Le sujet propose un choix entre trois formats (discours, essai, lettre) dont un seul doit être traité le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles fournis illustrent chacun des choix possibles pour couvrir l'ensemble du barème, mais un candidat ne rédige normalement qu'un seul de ces textes.
